name: Hakkatan
title: Father of Johanan, a returning exile
summary: Hakkatan is mentioned in the book of Ezra as the father of Johanan, who led a group from the descendants of Asaph (the clan of Azgad) back to Jerusalem from Babylon under Ezra's leadership. He is one of the family heads who returned to the Promised Land after the exile, representing loyalty to God's people and their homeland.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the list of returning exiles
keyEvents.description: Hakkatan is mentioned as the father of Johanan, who led 110 men from the clan of Azgad back to Jerusalem from Babylon under Ezra's leadership.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's caravan from Babylon
keyEvents.description: Hakkatan's son Johanan was among the family heads who gathered at the river that flows toward Ahava, to travel to Jerusalem with Ezra.

keyEvents.title: Fasting and prayer before the journey
keyEvents.description: The group that included Hakkatan's son Johanan fasted and prayed to God for a safe journey, as they were too proud to ask the king for military escort.

keyEvents.title: Safe arrival in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Hakkatan's son Johanan and the other returnees arrived safely in Jerusalem with gifts and temple equipment, protected by God's hand.

keyEvents.title: Parallel mention in Ezra
keyEvents.description: Hakkatan is also mentioned in the apocryphal book 1 Esdras in a parallel account of the return from exile, which confirms his historical role.
